text:
The finite provisional prototype is a qualified local draft only. W-D0–W-D4 and Sprint 1 stay open. SP01.6 stays blocked. This is the Grok 4.7 xhigh seat on the frozen bytes; it does not re-execute K, Quint, or Node, and it does not speak for GPT-6 Sol.

Sampled single-fault success rules do line up. Transfer with `f>0` is debit `v+f`, credit `v`, credit `f`, gross allowance use, one replay consumption, one head advance, work `-1/+1`. Zero fee omits the fee line in the TypeScript preparer (`mil4-s0-core-v5.ts:206-209`), the K zero-fee rule (`s0.k:108-111`), and Quint `transferLines` (`s0.qnt:97-107`). Repay is accrual-first: `da=min(n,accrued)`, `dp=n-da`, debit `n`, credit the obligation-bound creditor `n`, outstanding' `= principal'+accrued'`, settled exactly when that hits 0 (`mil4-s0-core-v5.ts:228-243`, `s0.k:117-124` and `250-261`, `s0.qnt:111-128`). Source formation is closed and ordered: exact raw profile token, action-shaped balance rows, `outstanding=principal+accrued`, nominal `2^127-1` versus state `2^128-1`, consumed replay left for history (`financial-agreement-source-v6-frontend.ts:221-222`, `251-301`). The wrapper withholds a prepared candidate when `signed_action` and `submit` differ and reports intent (`mil4-s0-source-v6.ts:40-51`). Pipeline order stage → intent → effect → authority → history is present in K and Quint; history checks stale head before replay in all three. None of that is signature validity, native proof, ledger acceptance, or full-state refinement. K and Quint premises are stipulated. TypeScript returns `PreparedUnqualified` and lists premises it does not evaluate (`mil4-s0-core-v5.ts:268-277`). `projection.md:3` still places ledger-committed `α` outside these runs, and its committed domain is empty.

## High

1. Within-intent first code diverges, and K’s repay alias rule is dead. The contract lists scope (endpoints, nonce, bounds, validity) before alias (`s0-implementation-contract.md:31-32`). Quint folds caps, round, and `claimedHead!=preHead` into `S0_INTENT_SCOPE` before alias (`s0.qnt:148-175`). TypeScript checks the round window first (`mil4-s0-core-v5.ts:165-172`), then alias (`190-191`), then caps (`194`). K returns alias as soon as `matchingScope` holds and `distinct` fails, before round and amounts (`s0.k:163-165` versus `168-174`). For repay, `distinct` is constantly true (`s0.k:172`), so K never emits `S0_INTENT_ALIAS`. Payer=creditor fails `goodDebt` / `stageShape` and becomes `S0_STAGE_UNSUPPORTED` (`s0.k:83-87`, `152-155`, `142`). TypeScript core classifies that same pair as `S0_EFFECT_RANGE` (`mil4-s0-core-v5.ts:224-226`). Quint classifies it as `S0_INTENT_ALIAS` because `beforeEffect` is called with `o.creditor` (`s0.qnt:254-256`, `171-175`). Source/6 formation rejects it earlier as `SOURCE6_CELL_SHAPE` (`financial-agreement-source-v6-frontend.ts:290-296`). One condition, four outcomes.

2. Within-effect order diverges, and several typed-cell failures change judgment. K and TypeScript return `S0_EFFECT_RANGE` before `S0_EFFECT_MISMATCH` (`s0.k:176-180`, `mil4-s0-core-v5.ts:198-201` then `252-253`). The contract table lists mismatch before range (`s0-implementation-contract.md:33-34`). Quint returns mismatch inside `beforeEffect` (`s0.qnt:176-177`) and only then balance overflow (`s0.qnt:218-225`, repay `258-264`). A missing fee line plus an overflowing receiver is therefore mismatch in Quint and range in K/TypeScript. The 14 shared fixtures never combine those faults. A settled obligation is stage in TypeScript (`mil4-s0-core-v5.ts:151-156`) and Quint (`s0.qnt:246-252`), and effect-range in K because `effectRange` requires `"Outstanding"` and the range rule wins (`s0.k:193-198`, `178-179`). Debtor≠signer is stage in TypeScript (`mil4-s0-core-v5.ts:151-156`), authority in K (`s0.k:208-212`) and Quint (`s0.qnt:265-271`). The authority row of the contract is the signer/payer mismatch row (`s0-implementation-contract.md:35`). Non-identity conversion is intent in K (`s0.k:101-104`) and authority in Quint (`s0.qnt:268-271`). TypeScript has no conversion field. K transfer `stageShape` does not bind endpoint names (`s0.k:150-151`); a missing signed balance cell fails `effectRange` and is reported as `S0_EFFECT_RANGE`. TypeScript and Quint report stage (`mil4-s0-core-v5.ts:142-147`, `s0.qnt:207-213`).

3. Head-extension codes diverge. Equal post and current head is `S0_HISTORY_STALE` in TypeScript (`mil4-s0-core-v5.ts:262-265`). K uses a third code, `S0_HISTORY_SUCCESSOR`, absent from the contract table (`s0.k:224`, `232-233`). Quint’s only successor is `preHead+1` / `currentHead+1` (`s0.qnt:107`, `127`, `364`). A non-increment successor becomes an effect mismatch against `transferLines`, not a history result. `S1-FINITE-CORRESPONDENCE.md:31` records opaque-versus-integer heads and stops there.

4. K positive evidence does not check financial post-state. `run.py:141-145` treats any stdout containing `accepted(` and no `rejected(` as a match. Amounts, obligation fields, allowance, replay, and head are unchecked. `results.json` is not in the frozen manifest. Quint’s witness source does assert post-cells for T-10-1, R-30, and R-near-bound; that is still one stipulated trace each. `S1-FINITE-CORRESPONDENCE.md:27` already records unequal pre-states (allowance 11/100/100, work 1/3/10) and says `α` equality is not shown. The table’s “Accepted” alignment is stronger than the K checker.

## Medium

5. `post_head` is an EBNF literal (`financial-agreement-source-v6-grammar.ebnf:44-45`) and the profile says every such literal is reserved (`financial-agreement-source-v6.md:9`). The reserved set omits it (`financial-agreement-source-v6-frontend.ts:11`), so `id()` accepts it (`164`).

6. Lowering stores the action id in `intent.programId` (`financial-agreement-source-v6-frontend.ts:336`). The spec maps the agreement identifier to `ProgramId` and the action id to `SelectedProgram`. Agreement id, settlement scale, and authenticated predecessor stay on the AST and off `S0State` (`327-332`). The wrapper labels those bindings unverified (`mil4-s0-source-v6.ts:13`, `57`). K state has no round and no predecessor (`s0.k:13`). Replay is a JSON text triple in TypeScript, a K constructor, and a Quint tuple.

7. Failure judgment and diagnostic work disagree. TypeScript’s judgment union includes `failure` (`mil4-s0-core-v5.ts:48`) and every rejection sets `diagnosticWork: null` (`61`); `prepareMil4S0` has no failure path. K can return `S0_FAILURE_UNSUPPORTED` with work `1` (`s0.k:238-239`). Quint uses `diagnosticWork: 0` (`s0.qnt:90`) and code `S0_EXTERNAL_PREMISE_UNAVAILABLE` (`147`). K’s premise code is `S0_STAGE_PREMISE` (`s0.k:138`). The contract states the K/TS split and is silent on the Quint spelling (`s0-implementation-contract.md:30`). `S1-FINITE-CORRESPONDENCE.md:31` records the work-field gap.

8. Two-balance K `goodState` does not bind the allowance owner (`s0.k:75-76`). A wrong owner reaches authority (`208-212`). TypeScript missing signer allowance is stage (`mil4-s0-core-v5.ts:146`, `155`). Quint `seedObligation` admits principal/accrued/outstanding up to `2^128-1` (`s0.qnt:314-316`); the repay path later applies the nominal cap (`246-252`). K `goodDebt` applies `nominal` at stage (`s0.k:83-85`).

9. Corpus holes on rules that do exist: no K/Quint zero-fee witness, no K/Quint full-settlement witness, no hostile net-floor witness, no K work-exhaustion witness, no alias fixture, no shared pre-state. Quint `replayTest` / `staleHeadTest` assert `History` and do not assert `S0_HISTORY_REPLAY` versus `S0_HISTORY_STALE` (`s0_witnesses.qnt` `replayTest` around the `judgment == History` expect). A swapped history order still satisfies those expects. The TypeScript “later partial repayment” test is a fresh document, not a second commit on post-state. H-nominal is source-only, as `RESULTS.md` says. `projection.md:3` still says no K-to-Quint projection has run.

10. Version identities differ: TypeScript stamps `moriarty-intent/3` (`mil4-s0-core-v5.ts:4`, lowering at `financial-agreement-source-v6-frontend.ts:335`) while K/Quint carry `Source/6` and `Core/5` only. W-D2 still has no `/3` bytes. The source profile text says a Source/5 `/6` rejection is unverified here (`financial-agreement-source-v6.md:7`); the test file asserts `PROFILE_MISMATCH` against a parser outside this manifest.

## Verdicts

Prototype: hold as an unfrozen local draft. Happy-path gross debit, fee-line omission, accrual-first repayment, bound-creditor credit, and the named single-fault judgments in the 14 overlapping fixtures are structurally aligned. The draft is not accepted correspondence. High defects 1–4 are executable disagreements or evidence that does not carry the financial claim. Stipulated `authenticated(...)`, `signatureVerified`, `nativeQualified`, and `ledgerAtomicReady` stay assumptions.

W-D0–W-D4 and Sprint 1: cannot close. W-D0 has no frozen shared fixture and no K post-state check. W-D1 and W-D2 have no digest, verifier, `/3` bytes, or round trip. W-D3 is the open leaf the three artifacts have already resolved differently (alias, effect order, absent cells, successor code, failure, diagnostic work). W-D4 has one near-bound repay shape in the rule texts and Quint/TS expects; Quint can seed non-nominal debt, and K’s harness would accept a wrong near-bound `accepted(` term. `S1-FINITE-CORRESPONDENCE.md:27-31` already lists the next `α` obligations as unmet. `decisions.md:3` leaves every normative row open. The disclosed README grammar failure is outside S0; it is not a reason to treat S0 as closed.

SP01.6: blocked. This packet does not supply signature validity, native proof, ledger compare-and-consume, or full-state refinement.

Dissent recorded: W-D3’s open status can be read as permission to differ. That reading supports keeping the draft provisional. It does not make the unlisted judgment splits a successful comparison, and it does not close the row. A second reading is that an external `results.json` might still show the right K post-state. That file is outside the frozen manifest; `run.py:145` would match a financially wrong accept. Direction Source/6 → Core/5, separate from `/3` wire bytes, still stands. No GPT-6 Sol vote is implied.
